sections.title: Investment Research Intelligence Agents
sections.description: For JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and New York's investment banking research community.

blocks.heading: Equity event monitoring agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents monitoring corporate actions, earnings announcements, SEC filings, and news for the companies in JPMorgan's and Goldman's research universe — generating structured event summaries and financial impact analyses for research analysts' daily briefings. The volume of market events that New York's equity research operations must monitor daily — across thousands of covered companies and dozens of markets — is precisely the workload that autonomous agent monitoring handles better than manual analysis.

blocks.heading: SEC filing extraction agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents processing SEC EDGAR filings (10-K, 10-Q, proxy statements, 8-K exhibits) to extract structured financial data, management commentary, and risk factor changes for the research analysts who track them — turning the thousands of filings per week that New York's research operations monitor into structured intelligence rather than document archives.

blocks.heading: Credit event monitoring agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents tracking credit events — covenant violations, credit rating changes, debt maturity schedules, and leveraged loan price movements — for the credit research and investment teams at New York's major banks.

sections.title: Legal Due Diligence Agents
sections.description: For Skadden Arps, Sullivan & Cromwell, Davis Polk, and New York's BigLaw community.

blocks.heading: M&A data room processing agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents processing acquisition target data room documents — extracting material contracts, IP ownership, regulatory approvals, employee agreements, and litigation exposure for the due diligence process that New York's large M&A deal volume generates. A complex M&A transaction may involve reviewing 10,000–100,000 documents; agent-assisted processing enables junior attorneys to focus on complex analysis rather than document organization.

blocks.heading: Regulatory compliance monitoring agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents tracking SEC, CFTC, OCC, NYDFS, and Federal Reserve regulatory developments for the compliance and regulatory practices at New York's largest firms — synthesizing regulatory updates into client alerts and practice group briefings.

blocks.heading: Litigation support agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents for document review and privilege logging in large litigation matters — organizing large document productions, identifying privilege and work product designations, and generating privilege logs for the major litigation practices at New York's top firms.

sections.title: Insurance Operations Agents
sections.description: For AIG, MetLife, Chubb, and New York's world-leading insurance community.

blocks.heading: Commercial claims coordination agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents coordinating the large commercial property and liability claims for AIG's and Chubb's commercial lines operations — gathering documentation, requesting additional information, coordinating with adjusters and defense counsel, and tracking claims milestones for the complex commercial claims that dominate New York's insurance portfolios.

blocks.heading: Regulatory filing agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents compiling and formatting the mandatory NYDFS filings for New York's insurance companies — quarterly financial statements, rate filings, form filings, and the annual statement preparation for the NYDFS-supervised insurance companies headquartered in New York.

blocks.heading: Reinsurance settlement agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents managing the complex settlement of reinsurance claims for New York's large reinsurance community — the inter-company communications, documentation requests, and settlement tracking for the reinsurance claims that Munich Re, Swiss Re, and New York's other reinsurers manage annually.

sections.title: Clinical Care Coordination Agents
sections.description: For NewYork-Presbyterian, NYU Langone, and New York City Health + Hospitals.

blocks.heading: Prior authorization agents for NY's payer mix
paragraphs: Autonomous agents managing prior authorization for New York's complex payer environment — Empire BlueCross BlueShield, UnitedHealth NY, Aetna NY, Cigna NY, New York Medicaid's multiple managed care plans, and the MLTC prior authorization framework that serves New York's large long-term care population.

blocks.heading: Post-discharge care coordination
paragraphs: Autonomous agents coordinating post-acute care for high-risk patients discharged from New York's large academic medical centers — the complex transitions to home health, skilled nursing, and rehabilitation services that New York's complex patient population requires.

sections.title: New York AI agent standards
sections.description: Key compliance standards for New York AI agent deployments.

blocks.heading: FINRA recordkeeping for all financial agents
paragraphs: New York financial agents serving registered firms must maintain FINRA-compliant records — ClickMasters designs all New York financial agents with FINRA Rule 4511 recordkeeping compliance.

blocks.heading: NYDFS oversight for insurance agents
paragraphs: Insurance operations agents for NYDFS-licensed companies must be designed with NYDFS supervisory examination readiness.

blocks.heading: Attorney-client privilege for legal agents
paragraphs: Legal due diligence agents must rigorously enforce privilege boundaries through role-based access control that prevents agent actions from breaching attorney-client privilege across matters or clients.
